    #50468. Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat

    📅 05 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2181 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat

    📅 05 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2181 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.
    • Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.
    • There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

    Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

    There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

    Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

    Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

    Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

    Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

    Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

    They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

    According to recent reports, even Chelsea’s in-house streaming had given up the ghost by the end. Consecutive pre-season defeats for Chelsea, but worth remembering that Colwill and Palmer sat out this fitness exercise and Enzo Fernandez is still to return. Palestra’s performances a real positive but the team is still finding its way.

    Juventus win a corner late on, but Yildiz’s delivery is too close to Penders. Just two minutes for Chelsea to find an equaliser.

    Mudryk does well to dig out a cross from the left but the goalkeeper Perin gathers. There will be four minutes of added time to play.

    Chelsea not really threatening an equaliser as the game meanders towards a conclusion. Should they score a goal, we will have a penalty shoot-out.

    Estevao looked for Mudryk with a reverse pass between full-back and centre-back but there was too much weight on the ball.

    Estevao’s free-kick is saved but the bigger news for Chelsea fans is that Mykhailo Mudryk has been introduced from the bench, replacing Nicolas Jackson for the closing stages.

    Sources indicate that lavia and Liam Delap involved in some handbags with the Juventus players, Bremer the centre-back in the thick of things too and has been shown a yellow card. Chelsea have a free-kick, Estevao over it from 35 yards out.

    Just the one goal scored for Chelsea against top level opponents in pre-season, but I doubt Alonso will be panicking just yet. Chelsea play Milan this weekend before hosting Real Sociedad on August 15th in their final pre season friendly.

    Industry observers note that juventus goalkeeper Perin sells Nicolas Jackson a dummy so he can pick a pass into midfield. The Italian side controlling the game quite well since the goal, against a weaker Chelsea team.

    Chelsea’s younger players will have to dig them out of trouble in the last 20 minutes. There has not been much in the game, Chelsea have shaded it in general play without quite creating enough.

    The Kosovan winger with a first-time, left-footed hit from almost 25 yards, curled into the top corner. Nothing Penders could do about it.

    According to recent reports, more changes from Chelsea: Anselmino, Acheampong, Satpaev, Assugo and Delap the players on, replacing Hato, Palestra, Gittens, Caicedo and Pedro. Alonso finishing the team with his younger players on the pitch.

    Jonathan David slides a pass across the Chelsea six-yard box when there was a chance to shoot, but the flag was up for offside in any case.

    Penders does well to palm away an inswinging cross from Zhegrova, before Estevao picks out the run of Palestra on the break with a brilliant forward pass. Chelsea corner, cleared. Now Caicedo has been booked for a cynical challenge to stop a break, much like Douglas Luiz.

    Nicolas Jackson hacked down by Douglas Luiz after he turned on halfway with three or four Chelsea runners in support. Painful one for Jackson, and a yellow card for the former Aston Villa midfielder. Chelsea players not happy with that challenge in a pre-season game.

    According to recent reports, chelsea certainly have the upper hand in the game, quick feet from Joao Pedro to win a free-kick in midfield. If either team is going to score the game’s first goal, you fancy it will be them.

    This time Chelsea find Palestra with a ball over the top, but his shot at goal is at a comfortable height for the goalkeeper.

    Sources indicate that palestra popping up in a centre-forward position again, but his shot towards goal is not struck cleanly. The right-back at the heart of Chelsea’s attacking again.

    Two very different XIs out there for the second half.

    Penders replaces Sanchez in goal, Sarr on for Tosin, Estevao on for Quenda and Jackson on for Welbeck.

    For Juventus: Bremer, Perin, Zhegrova, Owusu and David are on.

    Not much to write/phone/WhatsApp home about, so far. The combination between Quenda and Palestra down Chelsea’s right has been the best feature of their football, am sure we will see Estevao on that flank in the second half among other changes. The bumpy pitch and a hydration break has not helped the spectacle.

    There will be four minutes of stoppage time, simply a result of the hydration break.

    Far too much space opens up between Chelsea’s defence and midfield, with Meritti turning and carrying the ball forward. Boga tests Sanchez with a strike from the edge of the box. That was probably Juventus’s most threatening attack.

    Palestra defends well as the last man up against Milik, Chelsea almost undone by Locatelli’s outside of the foot pass.

    Robert Sanchez caught under a cross swung to the back post, very unconvincing goalkeeping, but Juventus could not get their shot away in the box. Nicoll-Jazuli then did well to bring the ball away for Chelsea at the edge of the box.

    According to recent reports, chelsea have another corner, and yet again it comes from a right-sided attack. Chelsea are in ascendancy now after a slow start, but it is a very low intensity contest.

    Caicedo with a couple of threatening crosses from a centre-right position, but no Chelsea player can connect with them cleanly. Gittens’s dribbling down the left causing problems for Cambiaso, and he was the one attacking Caicedo’s cross at the back post.

    Play has now resumed after the drinks break. No changes from either team, those will come at half time. Chelsea have 21 players sitting on their bench, albeit a number of academy players are on tour.

    Time for a hydration break, even though the game is being played under a closed roof.

    Recent findings suggest that chelsea’s right side is their most dangerous, by a distance. Quenda does well to slip Palestra in on the overlap, and his low cross into the six-yard box is cleared for a corner. Juventus clear. Boga with a burst through the Chelsea midfield but the Juventus man then gets his pass wrong.

    In a recent development, kelly with a left-to-right switch to Cambiaso, and his cross deflects off the toe of Miretti in the middle and trickles just wide of the far post. Sanchez was scrambling but I think the goalkeeper had it covered.

    Chelsea enjoying their most sustained spell of possession in Juventus’s half so far, without quite carving out a clear cut chance. Juventus defending their penalty area with a back five, but they do not have Bonucci, Chiellini and Barzagli back there anymore.

    Quenda with a threatening inswinging cross from the right flank, but Welbeck could not quite rise high enough to direct his header towards the far corner. Quenda was keeping the width for Chelsea with Palestra inside the winger in the box. Quenda then slices a shot over from long range.

    Welbeck and Caicedo involved in some good combination play, with Nicoll-Jazuli’s outside of the foot pass finding Gittens. Chelsea’s left-winger runs into traffic, but he has been one of the bright spots of the pre-season campaign thus far.

    It has been revealed that having watched a couple of Chelsea’s friendlies, there is a lot to like about Palestra at right-back. Tall, long stride, lots of composure on the ball. Will be interesting to see if they can find a way for him and Reece James to start games. Chelsea as a team yet to find much rhythm in the game so far.

    Tosin could well find himself down the pecking order this season among Chelsea’s raft of centre-backs, but he makes an crucial block in the area before Locatelli drags a shot wide from the edge of the box.

    Recent findings suggest that former Bournemouth defender Lloyd Kelly is in the Juventus team. The Italian team are looking to press high in the early minutes whenever Chelsea try to play out from the back. Quenda with an early dart at the Juventus defence but he gets the pass all wrong with Palestra overlapping.

    In a recent development, palestra with a loose first touch but he recovers and defends well. Like in Sydney, this looks another very bumpy pitch, you can see the join marks between the pieces of turf that have been freshly laid. Coming out of these games without any injuries will be a priority for Alonso.

    Juventus get the game started in their pale pink away kit.

    Juventus XI: Di Gregorio, Kalulu, Gatti, Kelly, Cambiaso, Douglas Luiz, Locatelli, Miretti, Boga, Milik, Celik.

    Subs: Perrin, Pinsoglio, Nava, Bremmer, Rugani, Koopmeiners, Arthur Melo, Cabal, Owusu, Gil Puche, Oboavwoduo, Licina, Durmisi, Yildiz, Zhegrova, David.

    Welbeck starts against Juventus, but no Jordan Henderson with the group just yet. As Sam Dean writes here: “Last season, especially, provided evidence that the balance of their squad was not right, and they are now trying to change the internal dynamic by adding more leadership and experience to the team.”.

    Industry observers note that how long will he stay there? Will he play his way back into Alonso’s team, be shipped out on loan or sold for a fee? Sam Dean assesses the options for player and club in this piece. Out of sight, out of mind could well be the most likely outcome for a player who has missed almost two years of football, and looked extremely raw before his ban.

    Looks like a back four once again for Alonso, and Danny Welbeck makes his first Chelsea appearance. Pedro will play off Welbeck as a second striker. Geovany Quenda was signed last year from Sporting CP, but joined up with Chelsea this summer. Another wide forward in their collection.

    Chelsea XI: Sanchez; Palestra, Fofana, Tosin, Hato; Caicedo, Nicoll-Jazuli; Quenda, Joao Pedro, Gittens; Welbeck.

    Chelsea subs: Penders, Sharman-Lowe, Curd, Slonina, Acheampong, Subuloye, Sarr, Diakite, Anselmino, Lavia, Essugo, Watson, Walsh, Kellyman, Mudryk, Estevao Willian, Kavuma-McQueen, Neto, Satpayev, Jackson, Delap.

    The wheels of commerce continue to turn for Chelsea in the transfer market but this afternoon Xabi Alonso’s team continue their preparations for the newly introduced season against Juventus in Hong Kong.

    It has been revealed that they have the chance to recover from the ignominy of losing to 10-man Tottenham Hotspur in Sydney on Saturday, but with 19 days until Chelsea’s Premier League opener against Fulham these matches are still a fitness building exercise. The positive from the Spurs game was Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Cole Palmer completing 80 minutes – three players who endured injury problems last season.

    Another new arrival is expected to follow Morgan Rogers, Marco Palesta, Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck to Stamford Bridge, with the club nearing a deal for Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria.

    It wouldn’t be Chelsea without talk of some eye-catching outgoings, with Spurs reportedly interested in Nicolas Jackson and Enzo Maresca eyeing a reunion with Pedro Neto at Manchester City.

    Alonso’s team promise to be flexible in their tactical approach this season, but so far he has set up with a back four rather than the 3-4-2-1 system he used to such great effect at Bayer Leverkusen. That could change as availability increases closer to the start of the season, but Palestra’s bursts forward from right-back in tandem with Estevao have caught the eye.

    In a recent development, juventus finished sixth in Serie A last season under Luciano Spalletti, the former Roma and Napoli coach who usually guarantees expansive and attractive football. Turkey left-winger Kenan Yildiz was their top goalscorer last season, and it looks like they will make it through the summer without the left-winger being picked off by one of the Premier League’s elite. Yildiz scored 11 goals in all competitions, and Dusan Vlahovic was the only other player to reach double figures so scoring goals is a problem to address. Lois Openda and Randal Kolo Muani have been signed this summer to strengthen the forward line.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Retail investors with access to Anthropic's initial public offering who sell the stock quickly after buying could get penalized by their brokerage firm.
    • Anthropic said in an IPO prospectus that it expected to make shares available to retail investors through various brokerages, including Charles Schwab, Fidelity, Robinhood, SoFi, E*Trade and some of their respective affiliates.
    • Follow CNBC's live coverage of Anthropic's IPO and Nasdaq debut.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Retail investors with access to Anthropic's initial public offering who sell the stock quickly after buying could get penalized by their brokerage firm.

    Anthropic said in an IPO prospectus that it expected to make shares available to retail investors through various brokerages, including Charles Schwab, Fidelity, Robinhood, SoFi, E*Trade and some of their respective affiliates.

    Follow CNBC's live coverage of Anthropic's IPO and Nasdaq debut.

    It has been revealed that these broker-dealers have different "anti-flipping" policies meant to discourage investors who purchase IPO shares — including those of Anthropic — from dumping them quickly. Charles Schwab is the only one that doesn't have such a policy in place.

    "One purpose is to discourage 'flippers' who are just buying with the hope of making a quick profit," Jay Ritter, director of The IPO Initiative at the University of Florida, remarked in an email. "Their selling could put downward pressure on the price once trading starts.".

    In a recent development, investors who run afoul of anti-flipping rules may be prohibited from accessing future IPOs, perhaps for several months or even more than a year for repeat offenders. In the worst case, the brokerage may bar them from all future IPOs.

    These policies apply only to retail investors who place an order with their brokerage firm to buy the Anthropic IPO at its offering price — something many investors don't have access to.

    Industry observers note that for example, Fidelity customers are eligible to participate in the Anthropic IPO if they have at least $25,000 in certain assets, the firm said. Even then, customers are "evaluated and ranked" based on factors like account assets to determine who can access limited shares that may be available, it said.

    Importantly, anti-flipping policies don't apply to retail investors who access shares later, once Anthropic stock starts trading on a public exchange, Ritter noted.

    Of the retail brokerage firms listed in Anthropic's prospectus, Charles Schwab appears to be the only one without an explicit anti-flipping policy.

    Industry observers note that "At this time, Schwab does not apply a flipping restriction to any IPOs unless required by an issuer," Margaret Farrell, a organization spokesperson, wrote in an email. "This is subject to change at Schwab's discretion.".

    She confirmed that an anti-flipping policy doesn't apply to the Anthropic IPO.

    Other firms aren't as lenient, however.

    Here's how they could penalize IPO flippers.

    E*TRADE said it "prefers investors hold shares for at least 30 calendar days.".

    However, its policy doesn't lay out an explicit penalty for failing to do so.

    Selling or transferring out of an IPO within 30 days "may affect eligibility to participate in other new issues in the future," according to its policy. "E*TRADE reserves the right to exclude customers from future participation," it added.

    Investors who are allocated Anthropic shares and sell within the first 15 calendar days from the start of trading in the secondary market won't be able to participate in future stock IPOs through Fidelity for a defined period of time, it said:.

    "The first day clients can sell without being labeled a 'flipper' is the 16th calendar day after the IPO trades," Fidelity remarked.

    Robinhood's policy stipulates that selling IPO shares within 30 days of the IPO is considered flipping.

    Such investors "may be prevented from participating in IPO access for 60 days," it mentioned.

    SoFi said that selling an IPO position within the first 30 calendar days after trading starts "may affect your ability to participate in future IPOs on SoFi.".

    It has been revealed that 1. Ja'Marr Chase (at WAS) - 93.5 proj. receiving yards.

    Chase is back to averaging 98 YPG this year after a WR1 overall stretch over the past month. The Commanders are a pass-funnel defense without a strong secondary. They've allowed the fifth-most passing YPG, and Chase hung 118-2 against them in his only game against Washington back in 2024.

    It has been revealed that 2. CeeDee Lamb (vs. TEN) - 90.5 proj. receiving yards.

    Lamb has been pretty up-and-down this year, but on average, he's the WR3 on WR2 overall usage as a no-doubt Round 1 value. He's leading the position in target share (39%) and air yards (145) over the past month, as the Cowboys defense has continued to allow anyone through the front door.

    Sources indicate that now he gets a dream matchup against a Titans defense allowing 35.0 half PPR points per game to WRs (first). They've allowed the most points under 20 air yards, specifically, where Lamb does almost all of his damage. They've been even worse of late without DT Jeffery Simmons and S Amani Hooker. Dallas enters as 8.5-point home favorites with a slate-leading 31.5-point team total (first).

    3. Justin Jefferson (at SF) - 82.5 proj. receiving yards.

    The Vikings passed more in neutral situations last week with Kirk Cousins compared to over the past year and a half with underwhelming QBs. That'll help Jefferson find his mid-range WR1 groove, on top of those throws being far more accurate. Jefferson had three screens last week, plus other underneath targets, allowing him to post a season-high 19.3 expected half PPR points (WR5). They didn't rip the explosive play, but those will be coming. In the short term, Jordan Addison won't be out there either.

    This week is a great spot for Jefferson. The Vikings are slight dogs, yet still have a 21.5-point team total in what should be a down week across the NFL. The 49ers were shredded by the Cowboys' pass game last week and have been given up 27.7 half PPR points to WR rooms on average this entire season. Most of those will go to Jefferson here.

    4. Amon-Ra St. Brown (vs. TB) - 76.5 proj. receiving yards.

    In a recent development, st. Brown was on a five-game streak without a touchdown before finishing last week with 23.8 half PPR points in Germany with a couple of long scores.     💡 Key Takeaways
    • Palo Alto Networks shares rose 6% on Thursday as businesses boosted spending on cybersecurity products and investors cheered the tech giant's acquisition of a startup that pushes it into securing open-weight artificial intelligence models.
    • The firm beat Wall Street's estimates for the fiscal first quarter.
    • In a recent development, recent outages at Microsoft, banks and the Federal Aviation Administration have left businesses reeling.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Palo Alto Networks shares rose 6% on Thursday as businesses boosted spending on cybersecurity products and investors cheered the tech giant's acquisition of a startup that pushes it into securing open-weight artificial intelligence models.

    The firm beat Wall Street's estimates for the fiscal first quarter. Revenue jumped 39% from a year ago and Palo Alto lifted its guidance for the year.

    In a recent development, recent outages at Microsoft, banks and the Federal Aviation Administration have left businesses reeling. While U.S. officials haven't detected any malicious activity, the disruptions raise concerns over aging equipment and infrastructure. Many businesses are scrambling to patch vulnerabilities at a faster clip than ever before to keep pace with the growing risks of AI-powered cyberattacks.

    Those fears have led more businesses to consolidate platforms, which is fueling growth in areas like firewall and AI security, Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora told CNBC's "Mad Money" on Wednesday.

    "They're going to have to make sure they get the best players in the market to come support them because this is no longer child's play," Arora mentioned.

    Sources indicate that alongside earnings, Palo Alto confirmed a $4.5 billion deal to buy Applied Compute, a startup that helps train customized open-weight models. It's one of several recent deals in Arora's aggressive acquisition spree and marks a significant shift beyond cybersecurity.

    "Rather than being one player out of 10 in the industry serving compute, we want to be the one player with Palo Alto that delivers secure compute and security capability," Arora told CNBC.

    Palo Alto expects the deal to add more than $1 billion in annual recurring revenue to its next-generation security business by the 2029 fiscal year.

    Analysts at Bank of America touted the deal as a "bold move" to expand beyond securing AI into training open-weight models, allowing Palo Alto to lead the next phase of the AI revolution.

    This "appears consistent with PANW's 'long-game' - become indispensable beyond cyber into multidisciplinary IT domains across AI-value-chain," wrote analysts at Citigroup.

    WATCH: Palo Alto Networks shares surge.

    Intuit to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (411 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that tax software maker Intuit said Thursday that it has agreed to sell marketing subsidiary Mailchimp to Italian technology consolidator Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion in cash and stock.
    • In a recent development, the sale is a costly retreat for Intuit, which paid $12 billion for Mailchimp in 2021 in a push beyond its core tax and accounting businesses.
    • The deal is the latest instance of Bending Spoons picking up a once promising technology asset.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that tax software maker Intuit said Thursday that it has agreed to sell marketing subsidiary Mailchimp to Italian technology consolidator Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion in cash and stock. The deal is set to close in early 2027, according to a statement.

    In a recent development, the sale is a costly retreat for Intuit, which paid $12 billion for Mailchimp in 2021 in a push beyond its core tax and accounting businesses. Five years later, the software maker is unloading the email-marketing company for less than one-third of that price after Mailchimp became a drag on its overall revenue growth.

    The deal is the latest instance of Bending Spoons picking up a once promising technology asset. The tech giant bought productivity software startup Airtable in September for 10% of what it was once worth.

    The Bending Spoons portfolio also contains AOL, Brightcove, Eventbrite, Evernote, Meetup, Vimeo, and WeTransfer.

    In August Intuit started running Mailchimp as a distinct operating segment. The move was meant to give investors more transparency as the manufacturer tried to manage the unit for profitability, Sandeep Aujla, Intuit's finance chief, said at a September company briefing.

    It has been revealed that also on Thursday, Intuit announced stronger-than-expected earnings and revenue for its fiscal first quarter, which ended on Oct. 31. The company reported $2.91 in adjusted earnings per share on $4.35 billion in revenue. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for $2.70 per share and $4.31 billion in revenue.

    While Intuit's revenue increased 12% year over year, Mailchimp revenue declined 1% to $313 million. Analysts polled by StreetAccount had expected $314.4 million.

    Sources indicate that management called for $22.88 to $23.12 in adjusted earnings per share for the 2027 fiscal year, with $23.081 billion to $23.365 billion in revenue. Analysts polled by LSEG had predicted $23.62 in adjusted earnings per share on $23.43 billion in revenue. Intuit shares tumbled 15% in extended trading.

    In a recent development, the manufacturer noted Mailchimp should produce $1.256 billion to $1.266 billion in fiscal 2027 revenue, which would be down 1% to flat year over year. In August Aujla said Intuit anticipated Mailchimp's higher effective prices offsetting increased client churn. Mailchimp was founded in 2001. Rivals include Klaviyo, which went public in 2023.

    Berkshire Hathaway invested $600 million in Bending Spoons when the acquirer went public in July, and in October Bending Spoons said Berkshire invested another $330 million.

    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Amazon app warns New York of higher costs if Mamdani delivery law passes

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (626 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Amazon is taking its fight against a Newly introduced York City delivery bill, which has been backed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani, to its shopping website and app.
    • Some users who open the organization's shopping app or website report being served with pop-ups and banners warning that the Latest York City Council "could add up to $5 per order" if it passes Intro 518, or the Delivery Protection Act.
    • Sources indicate that the bill would require Amazon to employ its army of third-party delivery companies directly, disrupting the contractor model it has relied on since 2018.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Amazon is taking its fight against a Newly introduced York City delivery bill, which has been backed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani, to its shopping website and app.

    Some users who open the organization's shopping app or website report being served with pop-ups and banners warning that the Latest York City Council "could add up to $5 per order" if it passes Intro 518, or the Delivery Protection Act.

    Sources indicate that the bill would require Amazon to employ its army of third-party delivery companies directly, disrupting the contractor model it has relied on since 2018. Amazon uses a network of thousands of small companies, which often work solely for Amazon, to handle the last-mile portion of shipments, in an effort to speed up deliveries and control more of its logistics operations.

    In a recent development, "If this legislation passes, we'd no longer be able to work with them, and we'd be forced to consider moving our operations outside of the city," Amazon's in-app message states. "That would likely mean slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers in New York City, while also threatening small businesses and their thousands of employees.".

    The proposed legislation was introduced in February and is awaiting review by City Council Speaker Julie Menin.

    It has been revealed that amazon also posted a statement on its tech giant website where it often publishes its policy positions. But rarely has the company used its valuable e-commerce site and app real estate to push its perspectives. Other tech companies including Uber and Lyft have similarly used their apps to advocate for or against legislation in the past.

    Amazon's pop-up notices and a stationary banner on its store homepage direct users to a form where they can "contact your council member to oppose Intro 518.".

    According to Amazon, 20,000 customers sent emails to city council members in the first six hours that the pop-up appeared.

    Menin told CNBC in a statement that Amazon's claim it will need to raise prices due to the proposed legislation "defies logic.".

    It has been revealed that "We are crafting legislation that regulates Amazon and protects workers, without impacting prices or jobs," Menin mentioned. "If Amazon thinks this deceptive campaign will effectively threaten Newly introduced Yorkers and intimidate this City Council, they are dead wrong.".

    Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel stated in a statement that the company put up the notices to be "transparent with our customers" about what the bill "would cause them if it passes as written.".

    "If customers are concerned, one of the most impactful things they can do is contact their City Council member and ask them to oppose this bill," Nantel mentioned.

    The Delivery Protection Act has received a swell of support from labor groups, including the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, which has sought to unionize Amazon delivery and warehouse workers.

    Mamdani endorsed the bill in August, saying Amazon's subcontractor model "leaves workers vulnerable and corporations free to avoid accountability for reckless conditions on city streets." He's argued the bill would lead to safer working conditions for drivers, and allow the city to "regulate last-mile operations.".

    Amazon disputed Mamdani's claims, saying the bill would put Delivery Service Partner jobs "at risk without improving safety." It also argued that other businesses and governments use contractors in their operations, and said the DSP model has allowed it to meet growing customer demand.

    "It works because local entrepreneurs — people rooted in their communities — deliver a better experience," Amazon mentioned. "They invest in their teams, their routes, and their neighborhoods. That's not a liability play.".

    Amazon has lobbied heavily against the bill, while logistics and business groups have launched local advertising campaigns, and warned they may sue the city if the bill passes.

    #50448. Jensen Huang's — and Nvidia's — legal exposure balloons

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1302 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Jensen Huang's — and Nvidia's — legal exposure balloons

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1302 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The still-unraveling scandal of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affairs and the tech giant's potential role in its advanced semiconductor chips ending up in China present a legal minefield for Huang and Nvidia.
    • Federal and state prosecutors and Nvidia employees may target Huang and the manufacturer in court, where some shareholders have already taken action.
    • That's on top of a rapidly growing pile of probes by Republicans who control Congress now and Democrats who will have majorities in both the House and Senate come January.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The still-unraveling scandal of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affairs and the tech giant's potential role in its advanced semiconductor chips ending up in China present a legal minefield for Huang and Nvidia.

    Federal and state prosecutors and Nvidia employees may target Huang and the manufacturer in court, where some shareholders have already taken action.

    That's on top of a rapidly growing pile of probes by Republicans who control Congress now and Democrats who will have majorities in both the House and Senate come January.

    "It's not going to get any better for Jensen Huang; it's going to get far worse," mentioned Salvatore Graziano, a New York securities litigation attorney at Bernstein, Litowitz, Berger & Grossmann. His firm is looking at shareholder lawsuit opportunities against Nvidia and Huang.

    [Huang] "faces the Department of Justice, the Securities and Exchange Commission and private litigation," Graziano said. "The criminal exposure is very serious. The SEC could bar him from being an officer. And the potential liability [from shareholder] lawsuits can be very large.".

    Recent findings suggest that huang's and Nvidia's legal exposure stems from three issues that led up to his shock resignation Nov. 12.

    Recent findings suggest that there's his alleged affair with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang, who worked for Megaspeed, a Singapore-based organization under investigation for diverting advanced Nvidia semiconductor chips to China in violation of U.S. export rules. That, in turn, has raised questions about whether Huang and Nvidia were aware of any diversions.

    There are Huang's two other alleged affairs with Nvidia employees.

    And there is the sharp drop in the tech giant's stock price in the wake of the scandal. Nvidia's share price has fallen 19% since Nov. 8, when Huang sent a company-wide apology acknowledging extramarital affairs.

    Huang last week retained the law firm Paul, Weiss and its attorneys Melinda Haag and Walter Brown to represent him. Haag is a former U.S. attorney in San Francisco, and Brown is also a former federal prosecutor.

    Huang's spokesman at Trident, a crisis communications firm, declined to comment when asked if Haag and Brown are representing him in any potential criminal case and other questions about his legal exposure.

    Sources indicate that nvidia did not respond to a request for comment. Last week, Nvidia retained the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent investigation into Huang allegedly being targeted by a spy, as U.S. intelligence reportedly has concluded.

    The civil liability Huang and Nvidia could face is underscored by a hearing Graziano, the securities attorney, attended Tuesday in U.S. District Court in San Francisco. A judge at the hearing approved a $175 million settlement from Seagate Technology Holdings to resolve a shareholder lawsuit alleging it concealed sales of hard-disk drives to Huawei in China in violation of export bans.

    The Seagate settlement came three years after the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security — which is investigating Megaspeed's business with Nvidia — imposed a $300 million penalty on Seagate for its sales to Huawei.

    Graziano said his law firm is "actively looking at securities law liability for Nvidia, Jensen Huang and other senior executives in the firm given all the recent developments regarding their [potential] knowledge and facilitation of illegal chip sales to Chinese entities.".

    There is already a pending class-action shareholder lawsuit in San Francisco federal court against Nvidia and Huang by the Rosen Law Firm, for allegedly misleading and false statements related to Megaspeed and Alice Huang.

    "Several hundreds of investors have contacted us and expressed an interest to join the case — investors of all walks of life, from mom and pops to investors with very large losses," Rosen attorney Phil Kim told CNBC in an email.

    Katie Sweeten, a former federal prosecutor in the DOJ's National Security Division, noted the question of "who knew what and when, and what was [Huang's] role" is potentially the biggest risk for Nvidia and him.

    "Now DOJ can leverage their criminal authorities," Sweeten, a partner at Scale LLP, told CNBC's Kelly Evans on "The Exchange.".

    "They can bring grand jury subpoenas, search warrants for emails, bank accounts, personal devices, computers, things like that," Sweeten said.

    While it is "not illegal to, you know, sleep with a spy ... it is illegal to pass certain types of information to a counterintelligence officer," she said.

    Sweeten also pointed to potential export control violations, which "could be very serious.".

    She noted the DOJ can indict a company as well as its officials if there is evidence of criminality. Export control violations carry a maximum possible criminal sentence of 20 years in prison and "really large fines," she said.

    "You can't send the tech giant to prison, but they can face fines, civil penalties, debarment — where you can't export items down the line," she said.

    One example of that came in July 2025, when the DOJ obtained a guilty plea and an agreement to pay more than $140 million from Cadence Design Systems for violating the Export Control Reform Act by unlawfully exporting semiconductor design tools to China's National University of Defense Technology, a school led by China's Central Military Commission.

    Another potential legal risk for Huang comes from his planned appearances before Congress.

    Huang is scheduled to give a closed-door interview Dec. 1 to three House committees. Senate banking committee Chair Tim Scott, R-S.C., wants Huang's testimony before that panel to be public, and told CNBC Tuesday he hopes to have that happen "before Christmas.".

    Sweeten noted Huang "has to be very careful" about what he says there because of the risk of being criminally charged with lying to Congress, and of saying something "that absolutely can become part of a criminal or civil investigation.".

    "I expect Huang to take the Fifth on most questions" from Congress, Jonathan Kanter, a former assistant attorney general in the DOJ's Antitrust Division, told CNBC, meaning Huang will likely use his constitutional right against giving testimony that could be used against him in a criminal case.

    "With a Justice Department criminal investigation into Megaspeed already underway and more investigations possible, anything he tells Congress could be used against him," Kanter noted. "His lawyers are likely to advise him against taking that risk.".

    Ben Heineman Jr., a former senior vice president and general counsel of General Electric, and a senior fellow at Harvard University, told CNBC that Nvidia's board will be scrutinized over its actions before it pushed Huang to resign.

    Heineman cited the board's apparent lack of succession planning and what looks like weak oversight of Huang, including relating to personal conduct such as the two alleged affairs with Nvidia employees and with an executive of an Nvidia customer.

    "When there is a sort of reasonable suspicion, they need to investigate it, and they don't appear to have done that," Heineman remarked.

    Nvidia and Huang could face investigation from state attorneys general, including in California, where the firm is headquartered.

    On Tuesday, California Attorney General Rob Bonta told Bloomberg Television that the situation at Nvidia with Huang is "something that we're interested in." Bonta's office later told CNBC, "We are monitoring the situation.".

    Huang's alleged affairs with Nvidia employees also open the possibility of workplace litigation.

    Ari Wilkenfeld, a Washington-area employment lawyer, said a consensual relationship between a chief executive and a subordinate "is not in and of itself illegal.".

    It has been revealed that "The liability never comes from the existence of the relationship alone. It comes from whether it was genuinely welcome, what job benefits flowed from it, and what it did to everyone else in the building," Wilkenfeld mentioned. "California law recognizes that so-called sexual favoritism can create a hostile environment for an entire workforce.

    "The affair is Huang's problem," Wilkenfeld noted. "What, if anything, Nvidia did once it knew is the organization's problem.".

    Julius Randle on Nets' 'embarrassing' blowout loss to Bulls: 'One of the worst games I've ever been a part of'

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1032 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that the Brooklyn Nets wore red, white and blue alternate uniforms on Wednesday night, throwing it back to the franchise's ABA heyday when they welcomed the Chicago Bulls to Barclays Center.
    • Recent findings suggest that "I fully anticipated the Nets to be so fired up having us here, they would blow Chicago out," the Hall of Famer said during an appearance on the YES Network broadcast midway through the second quarter.
    • The Nets scored Wednesday's first basket, with young guard Nolan Traoré getting a runout dunk after Egor Dëmin picked off a Josh Giddey pass.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that the Brooklyn Nets wore red, white and blue alternate uniforms on Wednesday night, throwing it back to the franchise's ABA heyday when they welcomed the Chicago Bulls to Barclays Center. The evening featured an appearance by 10 members of the teams that won ABA championships in 1974 and 1976 — including the legendary "Dr. J," Julius Erving.

    Recent findings suggest that "I fully anticipated the Nets to be so fired up having us here, they would blow Chicago out," the Hall of Famer said during an appearance on the YES Network broadcast midway through the second quarter. "But I'm looking at 62-39, so … I was wrong.".

    The Nets scored Wednesday's first basket, with young guard Nolan Traoré getting a runout dunk after Egor Dëmin picked off a Josh Giddey pass. A minute later, Bulls guard Norman Powell knocked down a 3-pointer to put Chicago on top … and, well, that was all she wrote for Brooklyn.

    The Nets never again led, or even tied, the visitors, trailing by as many as 37 points in a truly dismal performance that settled as a 137-107 blowout loss. At home. At the hands of what had been a three-win team, with the NBA's fifth-worst offense and absolute worst defense … and without exciting lottery pick Caleb Wilson.

    It was a wretched outing — one that saw the Nets commit 20 turnovers leading to 27 Chicago points, and allow 15 first-half 3-pointers and 76 first-half points, the third straight game in which they conceded 70-plus before intermission. Brooklyn gave up 62 total points in the paint, and sat idly by as eight different Bulls scored in double figures.

    In the midst of the depressing showing, courtside cameras caught Brooklyn forward Julius Randle lighting into his teammates on the Nets bench:.

    After finishing the night with 17 points, four assists and no rebounds in 27 minutes of work in the lopsided loss, Randle — who's soldiered through a 17-win season with the Lakers, the post-Anthony Davis doldrums in Newly introduced Orleans, and the 21-win end of the David Fizdale era in New York — sounded a similarly dour note about the state of affairs for the 3-11 Nets in his postgame press conference.

    "That was embarrassing," Randle said, according to Brian Lewis of the New York Post. "Been in the league for 13 years, and that's one of the worst games I've ever been a part of. And not because of the score … but it's how we did it. That wasn't cool. Nothing about it was cool. We've got to find a way to figure out the root of it or whatever, but that's just unacceptable. It's just a pride, an effort, the competitive spirit — all of that, it was nonexistent.".

    Sources indicate that the Nets entered Wednesday intending to celebrate the high-water mark in franchise history, but wound up closer to a historic nadir. According to Erik Slater of Clutch Points, the last two losses "mark the first time they've given up 135 points in back-to-back games since April 1 [and] 2, 1969.".

    According to recent reports, that's a far cry from where the Nets hoped to be after trading this summer for Randle, a three-time All-Star and two-time All-NBA selection who'd starred for the cross-town New York Knicks before helping the Minnesota Timberwolves make a pair of playoff runs, to pair with incumbent sweet-shooting forward Michael Porter Jr. in the frontcourt, in hopes of restoring a franchise that had the third-worst record in the NBA over the preceding three seasons to respectability.

    But despite the presence of the 20-point-scoring veteran forwards and some exciting flashes from young guards Traoré, Dëmin and rookie Mikel Brown Jr., Brooklyn has remained mired in the muck, ranking among the league's worst teams on both ends of the court and looking like a team without much of a sense of who it wants to be, how it wants to play, and what its path to success might look like.

    "Very disappointed, just starting with effort," head coach Jordi Fernández mentioned after the game, according to C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News. "We were not a competitive group. We were not a connected group. We were not a selfless group. I saw selfishness. I saw pointing fingers, and I saw guys that didn't always play hard.".

    According to recent reports, that's not the brand of ball that Fernández has preached since arriving in Brooklyn in 2024. The team's desultory effort, though, suggests that maybe what he's preaching isn't quite getting across.

    Sources indicate that "I can try to say it in Spanish, because in English, they don't understand," Fernández quipped after the game. "So I'll keep trying and find whatever language works. But yeah, our effort was not good.".

    Julius Randle didn't mince words when describing the state of affairs for his 3-11 Nets. (Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images).

    According to recent reports, if the coach's message is falling on deaf ears, then it's up to the players to stem the tide and turn things around. Randle appeared to be searching for a way to do so with his impassioned entreaty on the bench; with another game coming against the Orlando Magic on Friday, he says he and his teammates have to look within for the answers they're seeking.

    Industry observers note that "I think when you win, you find ways to win. When you lose, you find excuses. Seems like a lot of excuses," Randle said, according to Collin Helwig of NetsDaily. "So, you know, for me, I've got to go back into work. I've got to go back into the film. I've got to figure out — I've got to look myself in the mirror tonight, too, like everybody else, and figure out what I can do better. Not point the finger or anything. Like, I got to figure out as a man [...] that has played this game since a kid and love it, and has given a lot to me, I got to figure out how I can help the team and be better for the team. So, you know, I put it on me.".

    #50440. Trump bought Nvidia, Palantir, SpaceX in September as federal deals, White House ties grew

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (901 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Trump bought Nvidia, Palantir, SpaceX in September as federal deals, White House ties grew

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (901 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • President Donald Trump's investment accounts bought shares of Nvidia, Palantir and Elon Musk's SpaceX in September, around the time the companies secured major federal contracts and their executives met with the president, according to a newly released financial disclosure.
    • The 25-page filing shows 751 purchases and sales totaling between roughly $40.9 million and $148.1 million, according to a CNBC analysis.
    • Among the transactions were Palantir purchases before the firm received two federal contracts worth $42.5 million combined, according to contracting records, SpaceX investments shortly before and after a $946 million NASA contract expansion, and Nvidia trades as its then-CEO, Jensen Huang, cultivated a close relationship with Trump.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    President Donald Trump's investment accounts bought shares of Nvidia, Palantir and Elon Musk's SpaceX in September, around the time the companies secured major federal contracts and their executives met with the president, according to a newly released financial disclosure.

    The 25-page filing shows 751 purchases and sales totaling between roughly $40.9 million and $148.1 million, according to a CNBC analysis. Purchases accounted for at least $29.2 million and sales at least $11.7 million. The filing reports transactions in broad dollar ranges, leaving the exact amounts and value of Trump's holdings unclear.

    Among the transactions were Palantir purchases before the firm received two federal contracts worth $42.5 million combined, according to contracting records, SpaceX investments shortly before and after a $946 million NASA contract expansion, and Nvidia trades as its then-CEO, Jensen Huang, cultivated a close relationship with Trump.

    In a recent development, the trades underscore a striking feature of Trump's presidency: His personal fortune remains invested in companies whose fortunes his administration can shape. His accounts reported more than 21,000 trades in 2025, compared with roughly 500 during his entire first term. Recent presidents have generally divested individual stocks or used blind trusts to avoid potential conflicts.

    The White House has told CNBC previously Trump and his family have no control over the trades, which outside financial managers handle independently. The Trump Organization says the arrangement is designed to avoid even the appearance of a conflict. There is no evidence Trump directed the transactions or that his managers knew government decisions in advance.

    In a recent development, white House spokesman Davis Ingle said that Trump's portfolio is independently managed and that neither the president nor his family has any input on trades. "All investment decisions are made entirely by independent managers," Ingle told CNBC.

    The Trump Organization did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

    The timing was particularly notable at Palantir, the artificial intelligence software maker whose technology is used by U.S. military, intelligence and civilian agencies.

    Trump's accounts bought between $15,001 and $50,000 in Palantir shares on Sept. 2, followed by another purchase of between $1,001 and $15,000 on Sept. 9.

    A week later, the Department of Housing and Urban Development awarded Palantir a contract with $10.4 million in initial obligations for AI-powered grant oversight and fraud detection.

    Recent findings suggest that on Sept. 29, the Department of Homeland Security awarded Palantir another $32.1 million software contract, bringing the two awards to roughly $42.5 million. That same day, CEO Alex Karp joined Trump, Musk, Huang and other technology executives at the White House for a meeting on artificial intelligence.

    Trump's accounts also bought shares and debt in SpaceX in the weeks surrounding a major NASA contract award.

    In a recent development, on Sept. 1, the accounts purchased between $100,001 and $250,000 in SpaceX debt carrying a 5.35% interest rate. Eight days later, they bought between $1,001 and $15,000 in shares of the major NASA and Pentagon contractor.

    Industry observers note that on Sept. 18, NASA unveiled a $946 million expansion of its SpaceX contract, adding three astronaut missions to the International Space Station and bringing the agreement's total value to $5.92 billion. The agency had signaled intends for additional missions in May.

    According to recent reports, six days after the announcement, Trump's accounts bought another $15,001 to $50,000 in SpaceX shares on the same day Musk attended Trump's White House state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping. The filing does not show whether the purchase came before or after the dinner.

    The trades followed an even larger SpaceX investment in August, when Trump's accounts bought between $1 million and $5 million in the organization's debt just two days before he signed a policy aimed at expanding commercial space transportation.

    Trump's accounts also continued buying Nvidia shares as Huang drew closer to the president — a relationship now under congressional scrutiny over Huang's ties to a woman suspected of spying for China.

    The September filing reveals four Nvidia purchases totaling between $152,004 and $380,000, including two on Sept. 2 worth as much as $350,000 combined.

    Industry observers note that the accounts also sold between $1,001 and $15,000 in Nvidia shares on Sept. 24, the day Huang also attended the state dinner with Xi.

    The trades bring Trump's Nvidia transactions to at least 108 since his return to office in 2025, worth between $27.2 million and $97.9 million, extending a CNBC analysis published Monday.

    The relationship between the president and Nvidia's then-CEO has drawn fresh scrutiny after The Fresh York Times reported that intelligence officials warned Trump about Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. Trump has denied being briefed. Huang resigned Nov. 12 following revelations about his personal relationships.

    The September filing also shows substantial trading beyond the three companies. The largest reported transaction was a Sept. 23 purchase of between $5 million and $25 million in Vanguard Dividend Appreciation ETF shares.

    That same day, Trump's accounts sold between $1 million and $5 million each in Comcast, McDonald's, Home Depot and Fidelity National Information Services, along with between $500,001 and $1 million each in Nike and Constellation Brands.

    On the buy side, Trump's accounts purchased between $250,001 and $500,000 in TJX shares on each of two consecutive days, Sept. 15 and 16. They also bought between $117,004 and $330,000 in Tesla shares across four transactions, along with smaller investments in CoreWeave, Intel, Microsoft and Apple.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.
    • Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.
    • The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

    Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

    The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

    Industry observers note that but that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he noted.

    “We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

    Industry observers note that “All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”.

    Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he remarked: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”.

    Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

    It has been revealed that the importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

    According to recent reports, raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

    It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

    But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

    Industry observers note that only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

    It has been revealed that “We did the first one quite well in a lot of moments but the compete part – especially in and around our box – was not to the standards to win a football match against a good side. It’s better to give them [the goals away] in a friendly match than an official match. It’s always good when you lose a match in pre-season because it creates a bit more fire in the belly.”.

    Kepa Arrizabalaga will not want to watch Betis’s first goal back in a hurry. The Arsenal goalkeeper may have got a slight nudge as he came for the ball at a corner but he was all over the place and never looked even in the vaguest control of the situation. Rodrigo Riquelme scored at the far post after the ball sailed over the keeper. Arteta called it a “really sloppy goal”. With former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier having arrived on a free transfer as back-up to Raya, Kepa faces an uncertain future at Arsenal. Moments like this will not help his cause.

    He did not feature much last season but is probably best remembered for his torrid showing in the Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City in March. He looked as unconvincing here as he did then, as the former Chelsea goalkeeper also sliced a clearance in the build up to Betis’s third goal. Before then, Kai Havertz had turned over possession cheaply from which Nelson Deossa set up former West Ham midfielder Pablo Fornals to score.

    Arsenal need more creativity and firepower in attack, hence the interest in Vinícius and Atlético Madrid’s Julián Alvarez. Viktor Gyokeres again looked rather limited here and the likes of Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze are also still to report back. Yet one of the few, brighter aspects of Arsenal’s performances was the sight of the regal looking Riccardo Calafiori marauding forward from a very nominal left-back role.

    It has been revealed that if Arsenal are going to play more adventurously this season and try to ratchet up things in the entertainment stakes then Calafiori could have a big role to play, as long as Arteta can keep him fit. He can be a potent weapon galloping forward and there were clear glimpses of that here. Harnessing that talent while not compromising too much defensive security may be one of the manager’s challenges.

    In a recent development, louie Copley had only been on the pitch for nine minutes – a half-time substitute for Ben White – when the 19-year-old midfielder went down largely unchallenged with what looked like a troubling knee injury. Arteta admitted afterwards that the way the teenager fell to the ground was a concern and he looked in visible pain and distress as he was treated by the medical staff before being helped off the pitch.

    Industry observers note that the fear will be of some kind of ligament damage and Arteta confirmed Copley would be scanned on Thursday. “Quite worried to be fair for the kid because the mechanism doesn’t look very positive and the symptoms that he already has,” the manager said. “So we are going to have to wait and see for tomorrow’s scan. Touch wood that is not a bad one.”.

    It has been revealed that premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the latest season as they take on Spanish side Real Betis at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin, with this being the first-ever meeting between the two sides. This is the first time Arsenal have played a pre-season game in Dublin since August 2018, when they drew 1-1 with London rivals Chelsea, with Arsenal winning on penalties.

    In a recent development, arsenal beat Girona 4-1 in their opening game of pre-season, with new signing Christos Tzolis on the scoresheet in his first appearance for the club. After today, Arsenal have three more games, including the Community Shield, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry on opening night of the new season. They are closing in on a deal for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes, who is set to become one of Arsenal’s most expensive signings. Mikel Arteta’s side have been dealt a blow ahead of the season with the news that France centre-back William Saliba will miss an extended period due to a back injury. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

    Real Betis, under the management of former Manchester City boss Manuel Pellegrini, finished fifth in La Liga last season and have therefore qualified for this coming season’s Champions League after a 20-year absence from the competition. Pellegrini has led Betis into European competitions for five consecutive seasons, which includes losing the 2025 Europa Conference League final to Chelsea. They have been busy in pre-season action already having played five games up to this point. They have won four of the five, including a 4-0 victory over Lyon, with just one defeat coming against Granada.

    It has been revealed that they have a number of former Premier League players in their ranks, including Antony, Giovani Lo Celso, Pablo Fornals and former Arsenal man Hector Bellerin. Real Betis have already played a number of friendlies as they build up to the start of their season, which begins on August 21 when they take on Real Sociedad.

    #50434. Breaking: Congress passes bill to protect older investors from financial fraud

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (923 w)

    Breaking: Congress passes bill to protect older investors from financial fraud

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (923 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Bipartisan legislation aimed at protecting older Americans and other vulnerable adults from financial fraud has cleared Congress, putting it on track to become law.
    • Called the Financial Exploitation Prevention Act of 2025 and passed by the House in June, H.R.
    • Recent findings suggest that the measure will next head to President Donald Trump's desk.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Bipartisan legislation aimed at protecting older Americans and other vulnerable adults from financial fraud has cleared Congress, putting it on track to become law.

    Called the Financial Exploitation Prevention Act of 2025 and passed by the House in June, H.R. 2478 was approved by unanimous consent in the Senate Wednesday night — meaning no senators objected to its passage.

    Recent findings suggest that the measure will next head to President Donald Trump's desk. The White House did not respond to a CNBC request for comment on whether Trump plans to sign the bill into law.

    The bill would generally allow mutual fund companies and their transfer agents, which handle shareholder records and transactions, to temporarily delay paying out redemption requests when they suspect an older or otherwise vulnerable investor is being financially exploited.

    Recent findings suggest that "Financial exploitation can have devastating consequences for victims and their families," remarked Erin Koeppel, a managing director and government relations and public policy counsel at the CFP Board, the organization that oversees the certified financial planner certification. "This legislation fills an key regulatory gap that can help protect vulnerable investors before assets are lost.".

    The measure's congressional approval comes amid growing financial fraud among older Americans. Those age 60 or older reported losing about $3 billion to fraud in 2025, a 25% increase from $2.4 billion in 2024, according to the Federal Trade Commission's latest report to Congress on fraud among older adults, which was released in October. That amount is 400% higher than the $600 million reported lost in 2020.

    "Generally, we support all legislation that aims to prevent any form of financial elder abuse," remarked Bob Blancato, national coordinator for the Elder Justice Coalition, an advocacy group.

    Sources indicate that while just 6% of older fraud victims reported losing $100,000 or more in 2025, those losses accounted for 70% of the age group's total reported losses. The number of people reporting losses of that magnitude rose nearly sixfold to 6,769 in 2025, from 1,136 in 2020.

    However, because many scams go unreported, the FTC estimates actual losses in 2025 could have been anywhere from $13.3 billion to $119.5 billion. In 2024, the estimated range was from $10.1 billion to $81.5 billion.

    It has been revealed that scammers are increasingly targeting Americans' life savings by impersonating banks, businesses and government agencies, according to the FTC. The schemes often involve fabricated emergencies that convince victims to transfer money to supposedly protect their accounts from being compromised.

    Additionally, content created by artificial intelligence that can help criminals carry out schemes is becoming increasingly difficult to detect and easier to make, according to the FBI.

    Under the Financial Exploitation Prevention Act, mutual fund companies and their transfer agents could temporarily postpone payments when they reasonably believe a redemption request involves financial exploitation.

    This would apply to investors age 65 and older, as well as younger adults reasonably believed to have a mental or physical impairment that prevents them from protecting their own interests.

    Sources indicate that companies could initially delay paying out redemption proceeds for up to 15 business days. They could extend the hold by another 10 business days if they still reasonably believe exploitation already occurred, is underway or was attempted. State regulators, certain government agencies or courts could also extend the hold.

    The bill also addresses the use of a "trusted contact" — an individual whom financial firms can contact when concerns arise about an investor's account. That person may be able to intervene to prevent the fraud by reaching out to the account holder.

    Mutual fund companies that opt into the new protections would be required to ask customers to provide the name and contact information of at least one trusted contact.

    According to recent reports, the legislation would build on existing investor protections. Already, the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, or FINRA, permits brokerage firms to temporarily place holds on certain transactions if they suspect financial exploitation of an older or otherwise vulnerable investor.

    Recent findings suggest that additionally, FINRA requires brokerages to make a reasonable effort to add a trusted contact to accounts, although investors are not required to provide one. Many banks and other financial institutions also ask account holders for a trusted contact.

    In a recent development, separately, another House-passed bipartisan bill that aims to provide some relief for certain scam victims is awaiting action in the Senate. That measure, the Tax Relief for Fraud Victims Act, is intended to prevent people who lose money to scams from suffering additional financial harm through the federal tax system.

    The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 temporarily limited deductions for personal theft losses, and Trump's "big beautiful bill" of 2025 made those limits permanent. Some investment scam losses may still be deductible, but losses from some romance and impersonation scams generally aren't, according to a 2025 IRS memo. Victims who withdraw money from a traditional 401(k) or IRA may also owe income tax on the withdrawal and, if they're under 59½, possibly a 10% early-withdrawal penalty.

    Sources indicate that the Tax Relief for Fraud Victims Act, H.R. 9500, would repeal those deduction limits and waive the 10% penalty on withdrawals tied to deductible fraud losses. The House passed it 408-17 in September, and it was referred to the Senate Finance Committee. It's unclear whether the Senate will take it up before this Congress ends.

    "We would hope ... the Senate will join the House in passing H.R. 9500 to end another form of elder financial abuse," Blancato said.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Core inflation in Japan soared to a fresh high in 2026, coming in at 2.2% in October as higher energy costs and their knock-on effects pushed up prices in the wider economy.
    • Core inflation, which strips out prices of food, was lower than the 2.3% expected by Reuters-polled economists, but was higher than the 2.1% in prior month.
    • Headline inflation came in at 2.3% compared with September's 2.1%, while the so-called "core-core" inflation, which strips out prices of fresh food and energy, dipped slightly to 2.2% from 2.4% in the month before, government data released on Friday indicated.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Core inflation in Japan soared to a fresh high in 2026, coming in at 2.2% in October as higher energy costs and their knock-on effects pushed up prices in the wider economy.

    Core inflation, which strips out prices of food, was lower than the 2.3% expected by Reuters-polled economists, but was higher than the 2.1% in prior month.

    Headline inflation came in at 2.3% compared with September's 2.1%, while the so-called "core-core" inflation, which strips out prices of fresh food and energy, dipped slightly to 2.2% from 2.4% in the month before, government data released on Friday indicated.

    Recent findings suggest that energy subsidies for households expired in September, exposing consumers to higher prices brought about by the Iran war. Energy prices climbed 2.2% in October, a sharp spike from the 0.6% decline in September. Gas prices jumped 5.8% compared to the 2.4% rise the month before.

    Fuel, light and water charges also saw a considerable acceleration, increasing 3.4% compared to last month's 0.8%.

    Japan has reportedly approved reintroduction of energy subsidies in December to stave off higher imported energy prices as higher prices crimp growth, hitting consumption and net exports.

    Recent findings suggest that october inflation reading is likely to push the Bank of Japan toward another rate hike in December, despite an unexpected contraction in economic growth in the third quarter. Data from LSEG indicates that there is a 75% chance of a 25 basis point hike from the Bank of Japan."The BOJ is likely to look through the temporary weakness in 3Q GDP and focus instead on underlying inflation and wage dynamics," Ma Tieying, senior economist at DBS Group Research, wrote in a Monday note.
